claim: Regenerating a scenario response creates an exact-parent model revision, retains every earlier variant, and fails closed if the scenario or response changes before commit.
verified: The generation contract carries an optional bounded parent response snapshot
Local and remote adapters receive the prior response as labeled regeneration context
A successful regeneration appends a model-attributed revision to the same response identity
The new revision names the exact prior revision as its parent
Prior content, provider, model, run, author, and timestamp provenance remain retained
A changed response head makes a stale regeneration fail before shared mutation
A changed selected scenario remains protected by the P-16 exact-source guard
Concurrent sibling regenerations survive Yjs merge and converge to the same deterministic projection
A response from another scenario is rejected before a provider request is built
The product exposes Regenerate and a collapsed complete lineage instead of overwriting visible history
Production TypeScript and Vite build passes
limitations: No live paid-provider call or packaged pointer/keyboard interaction is included in this proof.
The product regenerates only the current response head; selecting an arbitrary historical parent is not exposed.
Concurrent sibling revisions are retained and deterministically projected, but no human conflict-resolution surface exists yet.
Regeneration does not score quality, establish truth, or apply policy text.
